articleHeadline: Varicella-zoster virus causes facial nerve damage.

articleHeadline: An incurable form of gonorrhea is spreading in Europe.
articleSummary: Untreatable gonorrhea is spreading across Europe, according to ECDC. Gonorrhea cases worldwide remain high: about 82 million new infections annually among people aged 15–49. In Europe, reported gonorrhea cases rose 303% over the last decade, with 106,331 confirmed cases in 2024—the highest since monitoring began in 2009. In 2023–2024, cases rose mainly among men (up 7.9%), while female cases fell 8.6%; 2024: men who have sex with men accounted for about 62% of cases, heterosexuals 37%. There is no clear solution yet for how to treat this evolving resistance.

The WHO has declared a public health emergency of concern. Suspected cases emerged in Brazil and Italy but were ruled out. Attacks on clinics and misinformation hinder surveillance and care; healthcare workers and three Congolese Red Cross volunteers have died. A humanitarian worker is under observation in a London hospital after potential exposure. The outbreak’s scale risks surpassing the 2014–2015 West Africa epidemic (over 11,000 deaths); concerns center on undetected transmission chains and insufficient surveillance. Veteran NHS emergency physician Dr. Simon Mardel cautions that lessons may not have been learned.

articleHeadline: Learn how to avoid bacteria in food, a threat in the kitchen.
articleSummary: Published 22 July 2026: WHO data link poorly stored foods to hundreds of millions of foodborne illnesses and over a million deaths annually worldwide, with backing from a University of São Paulo study (Brazil). The article presents eight kitchen errors and corrective measures to reduce microbial risk. Error 1: Reusing utensils for raw and cooked foods—use clean, separate tools. Error 2: Washing chicken in the sink—spatter can contaminate surfaces; avoid washing or sanitize nearby. Error 3: Waiting for food to cool before refrigeration—refrigerate while still warm. Error 4: Random fridge organization—top shelf dairy, middle leftovers, third items in process; produce in the crisper; door for beverages and condiments. Error 5: Exceeding recommended fridge times—fish/meat up to 3 days; leftovers 1–2; produce 3–7; sauces longer. Error 6: Storing meat in foam trays—transfer to plastic containers; freeze if unused in 3 days. Error 7: Washing produce with water only—soak in sodium hypochlorite solution (1 tablespoon per liter) for 15 minutes. Error 8: Undercooking meats or eggs—cook thoroughly to safe temperatures.

articleHeadline: Guiding neurosurgical intervention in tuberculous meningitis: evaluation of clinical features, laboratory parameters, and outcomes with a treatment algorithm
articleSummary: In a retrospective study at the Philippine General Hospital (Jan 2021–May 2025), 175 adult tuberculous meningitis (TBM) patients were evaluated to characterize the clinical profile and validate a logistic regression–based model for guiding CSF-diversion surgery in TBM-associated hydrocephalus. The cohort’s mean age was 37±15 years, with 61% male; 84% presented with Modified Vellore grades 3–4, and hydrocephalus occurred in 70% (n=122). CSF diversion was performed in 30% (n=53). Overall mortality reached 44% (n=77), driven by septic shock and brain herniation. The predictive model showed good discrimination (AUC 0.84; 95% CI 0.71–0.86). A recalibrated g-score threshold >0.20 improved balance (sensitivity 91.2%, specificity 60.8%, PPV 32%, NPV 96%). Altered sensorium (OR 6.89) and persistent headache (OR 4.26) were the strongest predictors of requiring surgery. The model offers a practical framework for surgical decision-making in TBM hydrocephalus, with utility in resource-limited settings.
